name: Applejack Still

angles.text: As a cook, you can distill and brew strong spirits from orchard fruit, a craft known among rustic cooks and tavern keepers across Azeroth.
As an engineer, you can see how mechanical condensation and plumbing turn fermented cider into concentrated liquor automatically.

faq.answer: The Applejack Still distills fermented apples into applejack, a potent spirit. Coils condense the vapor into clear liquor that pours into a bottle.
Concentrated apple vapor gives the still its sharp scent, strong enough to sting the nostrils. The vapor rises as alcohol evaporates and condenses inside the metal coils.
faq.q: Why is the apple scent so strong around the still?

faq.answer: The still pours a clear spirit into a bottle. This applejack is a potent fruit brandy made by distilling fermented apples.
faq.q: What kind of liquid does the machine dispense?

faq.answer: The still heats fermented apple cider or wash, separating alcohol vapor from water and fruit solids. Coils condense the vapor, and the spirit collects at the spout before filling a waiting bottle.
faq.q: How does the distillation device operate?

faq.answer: Applejack is a strong alcoholic drink made by distilling fermented apple cider. It is clear and aromatic, with more alcohol than ordinary cider or ale.
The still gives off alcoholic vapors strong enough to sting the nose. It dispenses clear liquor, but high-proof vapor and pressure call for caution.

sections.body: Fermented cider passes through the still and emerges as strong spirit. Near the apparatus, apple vapor stings the nostrils. Pipes and coils draw the fruit's essence and condense it into liquor.
sections.title: The Distillation Device

sections.body: Alcohol vapor condenses inside the still and becomes a clear spirit. Applejack flows from the outlet into a waiting bottle, ready to drink or store. Even in rough field conditions, the apparatus produces a clear, potent brew.
sections.title: A Clear Pour

summary: At the Applejack Still, cider becomes a clear, potent spirit. Apple vapor rises as the coils turn it into liquor.
